# Authorizer

> Authorizer is an open-source authentication and authorization server you self-host on your own infrastructure. It implements OAuth2 and OpenID Connect, adds fine-grained authorization (embedded OpenFGA), and ships auth for AI agents (built-in MCP server, RFC 8693 delegation). Every user record stays in a database you control—the "own your identity layer" alternative to hosted identity platforms, with no per-seat auth tax.

## What it is
- Open-source (self-hosted) authentication and authorization server; a single Go binary configured entirely by CLI flags.
- Standards-based: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect provider (authorization code + PKCE, client credentials, refresh tokens, discovery, JWKS).
- Auth methods: email/password, social login, magic link, WebAuthn passkeys, MFA (TOTP, email OTP, SMS OTP).
- Enterprise: organizations and multi-tenancy, SAML 2.0 (Service Provider and Identity Provider), per-org OIDC SSO, SCIM 2.0 provisioning, verified domains with home-realm discovery.
- Authorization: role-based access control (RBAC) plus fine-grained, relationship-based authorization with an embedded OpenFGA (Zanzibar) engine.
- Machine identity: service accounts, client credentials, and secretless workload identity (RFC 7523 JWT client assertions, SPIFFE, Kubernetes).
- APIs: GraphQL, REST, and gRPC, all generated from one service definition. SDKs for Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, and React (Python pre-release; Vue and Svelte beta).
- Operations: webhooks, audit logs, Prometheus metrics, rate limiting, customizable email templates.

## AI agents and MCP
- Built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at /mcp: MCP hosts such as Claude and Cursor sign users in with OAuth 2.1 and call profile and permission-check tools.
- MCP-ready OAuth: protected resource metadata (RFC 9728), authorization server metadata (RFC 8414), resource indicators (RFC 8707), Client ID Metadata Documents, and optional Dynamic Client Registration, behind a consent screen.
- Agent delegation: RFC 8693 token exchange issues a token carrying both the user (sub) and the agent (act), with scopes narrowed to what both are allowed.
- Agent-aware authorization: FGA checks for a delegated token require both the agent and the user to hold the permission; audit logs record the acting agent.
- Permission-aware RAG: filter retrieved documents by the user's FGA permissions before they reach the model.

## Key differentiators
- Data sovereignty: user directory lives in your own database, not a vendor dashboard.
- Database-agnostic: 17 backends across SQL, NoSQL, and graph (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, libSQL/Turso, SQL Server, YugabyteDB, CockroachDB, PlanetScale, SereneDB, MongoDB, Cassandra, ScyllaDB, ArangoDB, AWS DynamoDB, Couchbase, SurrealDB).
- Cost predictable: open source; pay for infrastructure, not per-seat usage.
- Deploy anywhere: Docker, Kubernetes (Helm), binary, Railway, Render, Heroku, Fly.io, Koyeb.

## Best for
Teams with data-residency or compliance needs (GDPR/HIPAA), cost-conscious developers avoiding per-seat SaaS pricing, engineering teams that want to own their authentication infrastructure, and teams building AI agents or MCP servers that need user-delegated, auditable access.
